paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God wasn't grading how hungry these people looked. He was looking at what their fasting did to the people around them. They said, "Why have we fasted, and You have not seen?" and God answered that on the day of their fast they did as they pleased and oppressed all their workers (Isaiah 58:3). Bowing the head and spreading out sackcloth and ashes was not the fast He had chosen (Isaiah 58:5).

So what does God want? He wants a faith that moves toward people, so He asks, "Isn't this the fast that I have chosen: to break the chains of wickedness, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free and tear off every yoke?" (Isaiah 58:6). Share your bread, open your home, clothe the one in front of you. I'm a stamper with a mustache, and even I know you can't polish your own halo while somebody next to you goes hungry.

And look at what God promises when His people live that way: their light breaks forth like the dawn, and when they call, the LORD answers, "Here I am" (Isaiah 58:8-9). He will always guide them, and they will be "like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail" (Isaiah 58:11). He also tells them to honor the Sabbath by not going their own way, and those who call it a delight will delight themselves in the LORD (Isaiah 58:13-14). So baker, when you open your Bible today, ask the question these people missed: not only "Did I show up for God?" but "Who got loved because I did?"
